[[No overall control]] | after_election = | after_party = }} The '''2026 Basingstoke and Deane Borough Council election''' was held on 7 May 2026, alongside the [[2026 United Kingdom local elections|other local elections across the United Kingdom]] being held on the same day, to elect 18 of 54 members of [[Basingstoke and Deane Borough Council]].{{Cite web |date=2025-12-22 |title=Council vote to go ahead with 2026 local elections |url=https://www.basingstokegazette.co.uk/news/25711884.basingstoke-deane-pledge-not-delay-2026-elections/ |access-date=2026-01-29 |website=Basingstoke Gazette |language=en}}{{Cite web |date=2026-01-20 |title='Democracy is precious': Councillors' plea to ministers over elections delay |url=https://www.basingstokegazette.co.uk/news/25775694.basingstoke-deane-borough-council-push-may-elections/ |access-date=2026-01-29 |website=Basingstoke Gazette |language=en}} == Background == In [[2024 Basingstoke and Deane Borough Council election|2024]], the council remained under [[no overall control]].{{Cite news |title=Basingstoke & Deane result - Local Elections 2024 |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/election/2024/england/councils/E07000084 |access-date=2026-01-29 |work=[[BBC News]] |language=en-GB}} The council was governed as a joint administration of the Independent Forum group and the [[Liberal Democrats (UK)|Liberal Democrats]]. The former consisted of the [[Basingstoke & Deane Independents]], other [[Independent politician|independents]], the [[Green Party of England and Wales|Green Party]] and the All In Party.
